claims.text: UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) is published by the Universal-Commerce-Protocol GitHub organization under the Apache-2.0 license with the copyright holder UCP Authors.
The ucp repository on GitHub was created on 2025-12-31.
Google introduced UCP on 2026-01-11 at the NRF retail conference.
At launch Google said UCP was co-developed with Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target and Walmart and endorsed by over 20 global partners.
UCP is not Google's Universal Cart; Universal Cart is a Google shopping product announced at Google I/O on 2026-05-19 that uses UCP for checkout.
In UCP the business is the merchant of record and keeps financial liability and ownership of the order; Google is not the merchant of record.
The UCP Governing Council has 5 seats: 1 permanent seat each for Google and Shopify and 3 elected seats.
Google holds the proxy vote for all open Governing Council seats until December 2028.
The Governing Council is the ultimate owner of UCP assets and Google acts as custodian of the ucp.dev domain.
UCP has no foundation; governance runs through a Governing Council and Domain Tech Councils defined in the organization's GOVERNANCE.md.
As of 2026-10-20 the Governing Council roster lists Amit Handa (Google), Ilya Grigorik (Shopify), Twum Djin (Stripe) and 2 open seats.
Stripe joined the UCP Governing Council on 2026-04-28, and 2 more elected open seats were added at the same time.
On 2026-04-24 the Tech Council expanded to 16 seats with new members from Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Stripe and Salesforce.
The 2026-04-24 announcement names Greg Smith as the Amazon member, while MAINTAINERS.md lists Greg Smith under Google and Jordan Williams under Amazon.
The Food Technical Council was formed on 2026-07-16 with Block (Square), DoorDash, Google, Toast and Uber Eats.
The Lodging Technical Council was formed on 2026-08-11 with Amadeus, Booking.com, Expedia, Google, Hilton, Marriott and Trip.com.
The Payments Technical Council was formed on 2026-09-02 with Adyen NV, Ant International, Coinbase, Global Payments, Google, PayPal, Shopify and Stripe.
Each Domain Tech Council has 16 seats, including permanent founding seats; the Governing Council elects members every 6 months and each council decides by majority vote.
Google holds 6 of 10 permanent Food Tech Council seats and 6 of 12 permanent Lodging Tech Council seats.
The Shopping Tech Council has 4 permanent members each from Google and Shopify plus 8 members from any organization.
Every UCP code change needs approval from at least one maintainer, and contributors sign the Google contributor license agreement.
A draft Lodging Booking capability, dev.ucp.lodging.booking, merged on main on 2026-09-24 (PR 780) and was announced on 2026-09-25; it is not in any release as of 2026-10-20.
UCP versions are dated identifiers in YYYY-MM-DD format, and git tags carry a v prefix.
The UCP releases are v2026-01-11, v2026-01-23, v2026-04-08 and v2026-08-25, and v2026-08-25 is the latest release as of 2026-10-20.
The GitHub release object for v2026-01-11 was created on 2026-01-23, the same day as v2026-01-23.
The v2026-04-08 GitHub release was published on 2026-04-09 UTC.
The v2026-08-25 release was published on GitHub on 2026-08-25.
ucp.dev serves latest and draft documentation channels, and on 2026-10-20 the latest alias points to 2026-08-25.
The AP2 extension was named dev.ucp.shopping.ap2_mandate from v2026-01-11 through v2026-04-08.
In v2026-08-25 the AP2 extension was renamed dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate when payment extensions moved from shopping to common (PR 741, merged 2026-08-25).
The v2026-08-25 release notes spell the migrated AP2 extension as ap2_mandates, but the schema name is dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate.
In a UCP release D every UCP-defined service, capability and extension declares version D, so core capabilities do not version independently of the release.
Third-party UCP extensions under com.vendor or org.org namespaces version independently of ucp.version and declare compatibility with requires.
The v2026-08-25 release notes describe independent capability versioning, while the normative spec pins dev.ucp capability versions to the release date.
UCP may backport backward-compatible changes into a published dated release, so two parties can hold different copies of the same version.
Breaking UCP pull requests carry an exclamation mark in the title and are announced in GitHub Discussions 2 weeks before merge.
Businesses must not advertise a non-date version such as draft in public UCP discovery.
Request and response signing was added by PR 156, merged 2026-02-17, and shipped in v2026-04-08.
Signals for authorization and abuse were added by PR 203, merged 2026-03-13, as a breaking change in v2026-04-08.
The Cart capability was merged on 2026-01-26 and catalog search and lookup on 2026-03-08; both first shipped in release v2026-04-08.
Identity linking with OAuth 2.0 capability-driven scopes was cherry-picked into the v2026-04-08 release by PR 431, merged 2026-05-20.
Web Bot Auth interop was merged on 2026-07-03 (PR 483) and released in v2026-08-25.
v2026-08-25 added the actions primitive, 3DS2 authentication actions, split payments, payment terms, location search and lookup, loyalty and permalink.
v2026-08-25 removed signing_keys from the profile schema and made the top-level keys array the only canonical signing key field.
v2026-08-25 changed buyer consent from fixed booleans to a map keyed by reverse-DNS identifiers.
v2026-08-25 split PAN and network token into distinct credential types (PR 424, merged 2026-08-22).
The main branch after v2026-08-25 adds draft capabilities dev.ucp.common.ask and dev.ucp.lodging.booking that are not in any release.
UCP defines a Platform as the consumer-facing surface, such as an AI agent, app or website, acting for the user.
UCP defines a Credential Provider as a trusted entity, such as a digital wallet, that manages the user's payment and identity credentials.
UCP defines a Payment Service Provider as the infrastructure that processes payments, authorizations and settlements for the business.
Payment handlers are specifications authored by credential providers, for example com.google.pay for Google Pay and dev.shopify.shop_pay for Shop Pay.
UCP defines the payment handler declaration structure but, as of v2026-08-25, no concrete handler of its own.
In UCP's payment model the credential provider defines the handler, the business configures it, and the platform executes it to obtain a token.
Businesses publish their UCP profile at /.well-known/ucp, and platforms publish theirs at the URI they advertise in the UCP-Agent header.
A UCP profile requires a ucp object whose version, services and payment_handlers members are required, and the services and payment_handlers registries must be present even when empty.
The capabilities member of a UCP profile is optional.
supported_versions is an optional business-profile field that maps older protocol versions to version-specific profile URIs.
Signing keys in a UCP profile live in a top-level keys array that is a JWK Set per RFC 7517.
The UCP profile schema forbids private JWK members such as d in published keys.

Each UCP service binding names a transport that is one of rest, mcp, a2a or embedded; in business profiles endpoint is required for rest, mcp and a2a bindings, while embedded bindings may carry a typed config instead.

Every UCP service, capability and handler entry carries a required version; payment handler entries also require id, business capabilities require schema, platform capabilities and handlers require spec and schema, platform services require spec (and schema for rest, mcp and embedded), and spec, schema, id and config are otherwise optional.
An extension declares its parent capability or capabilities in an extends field, which can be a string or an array.
UCP capability names follow the pattern reverse-domain, then service, then capability, for example dev.ucp.shopping.checkout.
The dev.ucp namespace is reserved for capabilities sanctioned by the UCP governing body, and vendors must use their own reverse-domain namespace.
Released UCP capabilities in v2026-08-25 include dev.ucp.shopping.checkout, cart, catalog.search, catalog.lookup, order and permalink.
Released UCP extensions in v2026-08-25 include dev.ucp.shopping.fulfillment, discount and buyer_consent, and dev.ucp.common.loyalty.
v2026-08-25 defines payment extensions dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate, authentication, split_payments and terms.
Common UCP capabilities in v2026-08-25 include dev.ucp.common.identity_linking, dev.ucp.common.location.search and dev.ucp.common.location.lookup.
A UCP checkout requires ucp, id, line_items, status, currency, totals and links.
Checkout status values are incomplete, requires_escalation, ready_for_complete, complete_in_progress, completed and canceled.
A checkout's expires_at defaults to 6 hours after creation when not sent.
The checkout links array is required and is described as mandatory for legal compliance.
The payment object is optional on create and update but required on complete.
A payment instrument requires id, handler_id and type and may carry billing_address, credential and display.
UCP credential types include a handler-specific token credential, a pan credential and a network_token credential.
The network_token credential requires number and cryptogram and may include eci_value and token_requestor_id.
The older card credential's card_number_type field (fpan, network_token, dpan) is marked deprecated in v2026-08-25.
A UCP order requires ucp, id, checkout_id, permalink_url, line_items, fulfillment, currency and totals.
Order adjustments record post-order events such as refund, return, credit, price_adjustment, dispute and cancellation with status pending, completed or failed.
Fulfillment events require id, occurred_at, type and line_items, with tracking fields optional.
A platform publishes the URL for order webhooks as config.webhook_url in its dev.ucp.shopping.order capability entry.
A cart requires ucp, id, line_items, currency and totals, and a checkout can be created from a cart with cart_id.
ap2.merchant_authorization is a JWS with detached content over the checkout without the ap2 field, in the form header..signature.
ap2.checkout_mandate is an SD-JWT with key binding that is required on complete and omitted on create and update.
The AP2 payment mandate is placed in payment.instruments[*].credential.token.

The UCP AP2 extension defines the error codes mandate_required, agent_missing_key, mandate_invalid_signature, mandate_expired, mandate_scope_mismatch, merchant_authorization_invalid and merchant_authorization_missing.
Signals carry observed values such as dev.ucp.buyer_ip and dev.ucp.user_agent and must not be buyer-asserted claims.
Platforms must send their profile URI with every request, using UCP-Agent: profile="..." over HTTP or meta["ucp-agent"].profile over MCP.
The UCP-Agent header uses RFC 8941 Dictionary Structured Field syntax.

A business computes the capability intersection, picks the highest version both sides list, drops capabilities with no shared version and prunes extensions whose parents are absent, repeating until stable.
Businesses must include a ucp field with the version used and the active capabilities in every response.
A capability's schema URL host must match its reverse-DNS name, which proves provenance but not trust.
Platforms must not fetch a schema URL whose origin fails the namespace authority check and must not follow redirects when fetching it.
Negotiation errors are invalid_profile_url (400), profile_unreachable (424), profile_malformed (422), version_unsupported (422) and capabilities_incompatible (200 with a UCP response).
UCP profiles must be served over HTTPS without redirects and with Cache-Control public and a max-age of at least 60 seconds.
Update Checkout is a full replacement of the checkout resource, not a partial update.
Without the AP2 extension, an agent may fill a checkout but must hand it to a trusted, deterministic UI for the user to review and place the order.
When status is requires_escalation the business must provide continue_url and at least one message with severity requires_buyer_input or requires_buyer_review.
continue_url must be an absolute HTTPS URL, and platforms must use it when checkout status is requires_escalation.
Complete Checkout returns completed with an order, or complete_in_progress for asynchronous processing with no order present.
During complete_in_progress the platform must not start a new Update Checkout or Complete Checkout operation.
A completed UCP checkout is immutable, and the business must send a confirmation email after completion.
A checkout session can be canceled unless it is already completed or canceled.
Payment runs in three steps: the business advertises handlers, the platform acquires an opaque credential from the credential provider, and the platform submits it to the business.
Payment credentials flow from platform to business only, and businesses must not echo them back.
A checkout submission must contain exactly one payment instrument unless the split_payments extension is active, otherwise the business returns payment_failed.
The authentication extension defines action types dev.ucp.common.payment.device_data_collection and dev.ucp.common.payment.three_ds_challenge for 3DS2.
The UCP authentication extension does not carry EMV 3DS messages; the business, handler and PSP own the 3DS state.
Once the AP2 extension is in the capability intersection the session is security locked and neither party may revert to an unprotected checkout.
With AP2 active, the business must include ap2.merchant_authorization in all checkout responses and must reject a complete request without ap2.checkout_mandate.
With AP2 active, the platform must verify the business signature before presenting the checkout to the user.
The checkout mandate contains the full checkout including ap2.merchant_authorization, so the platform's signature covers the business signature.
Over A2A, UCP checkout data travels in DataPart objects keyed a2a.ucp.checkout, a2a.ucp.checkout.payment and a2a.ucp.checkout.signals.
Businesses send full order snapshots to the platform's webhook with Standard Webhooks headers Webhook-Id and Webhook-Timestamp.
UCP order webhooks must be signed with RFC 9421, and platforms must reject events whose signer does not match the order's business.
Identity linking uses the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE S256, and plain PKCE must not be used.
Identity linking defines three access levels: public, agent-authenticated and user-authenticated.
Platforms discover the authorization server through RFC 9728 metadata, then RFC 8414 metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, falling back to OpenID discovery only on 404.
The accelerated IdP flow chains a trusted IdP identity to a new business with RFC 8693 token exchange and an RFC 7523 JWT bearer grant.
Identity linking scopes are derived from capabilities, for example dev.ucp.shopping.checkout:manage and dev.ucp.shopping.order:read.
Businesses that support identity linking must implement RFC 7009 token revocation.
The UCP REST binding defines POST /checkout-sessions, GET and PUT /checkout-sessions/{id}, POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/complete and POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/cancel.
The UCP REST binding defines POST /carts, GET and PUT /carts/{id} and POST /carts/{id}/cancel.
The UCP REST binding defines POST /catalog/search, POST /catalog/lookup, POST /catalog/product and GET /orders/{id}.
UCP MCP tools include create_checkout, get_checkout, update_checkout, complete_checkout, cancel_checkout, search_catalog, lookup_catalog, get_product and get_order.
UCP MCP tools also include create_cart, get_cart, update_cart and cancel_cart, and common tools search_locations and lookup_locations.
UCP specifies streamable HTTP for MCP so the same RFC 9421 signatures apply to MCP requests.
REST services are described by OpenAPI, MCP and embedded services by OpenRPC, and A2A by an Agent Card.
For the A2A transport the endpoint field is the business's Agent Card URL.
The UCP REST OpenAPI marks UCP-Agent and Request-Id as required headers, and Idempotency-Key as required on state-changing operations.
The embedded checkout protocol uses JSON-RPC messages such as ec.ready, ec.start, ec.complete, ec.totals.change and ec.payment.credential_request.
Reusing an idempotency key with a different payload returns HTTP 409.
UCP signs HTTP requests, responses and webhooks with RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures and binds bodies with an RFC 9530 Content-Digest using sha-256.
All UCP implementations must support verifying ES256 signatures, while ES384 and EdDSA support is optional.
Proxies and gateways must not re-serialize JSON bodies on signed UCP messages because that breaks the Content-Digest.
UCP handles replay protection at the business layer through a signed Idempotency-Key rather than signature timestamps.
UCP idempotency keys need at least 128 bits of entropy and must be stored at least 24 hours, with 48 hours recommended.
Web Bot Auth-shape UCP signatures add a Signature-Agent header, tag="web-bot-auth", required created and expires parameters, and a recommended nonce.
AP2 mandates and the merchant authorization are canonicalized with JCS (RFC 8785) because mandates are stored as durable evidence.
The UCP AP2 extension follows AP2 v0.2 signing rules for ECDSA (ES256, ES384, ES512) and notes an inconsistency in AP2 tracked as AP2 issue 268.
Webhooks sent from business to platform must be signed.
UCP supports authentication by API keys, OAuth 2.0, mTLS or RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures.
With API keys, OAuth or mTLS, verifiers must confirm the authenticated principal may act for the profile named in UCP-Agent.
UCP allows permissionless onboarding, so any platform with a discoverable profile can interact with any business without prior registration.
Businesses should keep a registry of pre-approved platforms and bound the cost of discovering unknown platforms.
UCP implementations must reject profile URLs that resolve to special-use IP addresses such as 169.254.169.254.
A compromised UCP signing key is not effectively revoked until it is removed from the profile's keys array.
Namespace authority binding does not consult the Public Suffix List, so entities should be declared only under a registrable domain the publisher controls.
The checkout spec says a business does not need to become PCI DSS compliant to accept cards through the checkout capability.
No GitHub security advisory existed for the UCP organization's repositories on 2026-10-20, and an NVD keyword search for Universal Commerce Protocol found no CVE naming UCP on the same day.

UCP's checkout schema has no spending-cap field; a cap can only come from outside UCP, for example AP2's payment.amount_range constraint in its payment mandate schema or a credential provider's token limits such as Stripe's usage_limits.max_amount.
UCP has no reputation mechanism for platforms or businesses.
Step-up in UCP comes through requires_escalation handoff and optional 3DS2 actions in the authentication extension.
Order adjustments can record disputes, but dispute handling itself stays with the business and its PSP.
Business profiles at /.well-known/ucp are public and cacheable, so anyone can see the capabilities, transports and payment handlers a domain advertises.

No public registry, indexer or explorer of UCP businesses was found in the UCP specification, the Universal-Commerce-Protocol GitHub organization or a web search as of 2026-10-20; the overview says reverse-domain naming removes the need for a central registry.
Google says UCP requests from its surfaces carry a UCP-Agent header and a User-Agent beginning with Google/UCP.
Google's endpoint health checks for UCP use the User-Agent Google-UCP-Prober/1.0.
The UCP organization keeps a public meeting-minutes repository created on 2026-02-04.
Sensitive data such as payment credentials and PII must be handled according to PCI-DSS and GDPR guidelines under UCP.
Google's FAQ says it retains standard order data shown on a user's My orders page indefinitely until the user explicitly requests deletion, while the merchant's own retention obligations still apply.
Google says the merchant's terms and conditions cover a UCP purchase and the buyer must accept them during checkout.
Microsoft's Copilot Checkout page says the merchant is the merchant of record and Copilot does not become merchant of record.
Copilot Checkout eligibility is limited to English-language merchants selling to US buyers in USD.
Senator Elizabeth Warren wrote to Google's CEO in a letter dated 2026-02-03, released on 2026-02-04, raising privacy, upselling and personalized-pricing concerns about Gemini checkout built on UCP.
The Python SDK ucp-sdk is on PyPI at version 0.5.0, released 2026-08-27, with 0.1.0 first published on 2026-01-12.
The JavaScript SDK @ucp-js/sdk is on npm at version 0.5.1, published 2026-09-02, with 0.0.1 first published on 2026-01-13.
The Rust crate ucp-schema, for runtime resolution of UCP schema annotations, is at version 1.4.1 on crates.io, published 2026-08-03.
The UCP organization hosts samples with REST servers in Python and Node.js and an A2A business agent and chat client.
The UCP conformance suite is a language-agnostic test suite whose README example targets ucp_version 2026-04-08.
ucp.dev lists 21 unique co-developer organizations across the Shopping, Lodging and Food verticals.
ucp.dev lists 51 endorsers, including Adyen, Amex, Mastercard, Visa, PayPal, Klarna and Worldpay.
The Shopping co-developers on ucp.dev are Google, Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target, Walmart, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Salesforce and Stripe.
UCP-powered checkout began rolling out to US shoppers for Etsy and Wayfair items in AI Mode in Search and the Gemini app, announced 2026-02-11.
On 2026-02-11 Google said Shopify, Target and Walmart checkout through UCP was coming soon.

Google announced UCP updates on 2026-03-19: saving multiple items to a cart at once, real-time catalog details such as price and inventory, identity linking so shoppers get loyalty benefits, and simpler Merchant Center onboarding.
On 2026-05-20 Google said UCP-powered checkout would roll out in Canada and Australia in the coming months and later in the UK.
On 2026-05-20 Google said brands that integrated UCP could let people buy on the spot from Direct Offers and Shopping ads on YouTube.
Google offers merchants a default native checkout integration and an optional embedded checkout for approved merchants.
Microsoft's Copilot Checkout requires a Microsoft Merchant Center account and a UCP-compliant feed.
Microsoft's page says Microsoft Merchant Center will support UCP, using future tense as of 2026-10-20.
Stripe documents UCP support with a Stripe Payments handler and says it is a member of the UCP Tech Council.
Adyen documents a UCP Tokenization Handler that follows the UCP 2026-01-23 tokenization guide and returns a token tied to a checkout session and merchant.

Shopify's help center says direct checkout in Google AI Mode and Gemini is activated by default for eligible stores (based in the US, selling to US customers, with a Google Merchant Center account) and can be deactivated in the Shopify admin.
The UCP repository had 3,438 GitHub stars and 480 forks on 2026-10-20.

No exact merchant count and no transaction volume for UCP is published by Google's UCP FAQ, ucp.dev or Google's posts as of 2026-10-20; Google's only figure is the order of magnitude it gave on 2026-09-16.
On 2026-02-11 Google said hundreds of tech, payments and retail companies had shown interest in integrating UCP.
Google told The Register it does not plan to take a cut of sales closed through its agentic checkout.
Google's FAQ says merchants need not support Google Pay on their own sites, but their PSP must be able to process Google's tokens.

Google publishes no fee statement or schedule for UCP checkout on its surfaces as of 2026-10-20 (its UCP FAQ and Merchant Center help carry none); the merchant stays merchant of record and pays its own PSP, which Shopify confirms for its merchants.
Checkouts in Google AI Mode, Gemini and Microsoft Copilot were reported to carry no additional fees for now, in contrast to a 4% ChatGPT checkout fee for Shopify merchants.
UCP checkout on Google AI surfaces supports only PAN_ONLY for the Google Pay allowed_auth_methods field.
AP2 is an optional extension used inside UCP, not the same protocol; UCP defines where AP2 artifacts go and AP2 defines the mandate formats.
Google's FAQ says AP2 can be used as a specialized payment layer within UCP.
Google donated AP2 to the FIDO Alliance on 2026-04-28.
On 2026-05-19 Google said it would begin bringing AP2 to Google products in the coming months, starting with Gemini Spark.
Production use of AP2 mandates inside UCP, or anywhere else, is unverified as of 2026-10-20.
The UCP spec does not mention x402, and no relation between UCP and x402 is documented.
Coinbase sits on the UCP Payments Tech Council, which is a governance overlap with the x402 ecosystem rather than a technical link.
UCP and Visa TAP both use RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures, but the UCP spec never names TAP and no bridge is documented.
No bridge or mapping between UCP and OpenAI's ACP is specified, although Stripe co-develops ACP and holds UCP Governing Council and Tech Council seats.
The UCP spec documents no relation to the Machine Payments Protocol, which Stripe and Tempo co-author; Stripe's UCP integration is a payment handler for tokenized methods.

Neither the UCP spec (v2026-08-25), ucp.dev nor Mastercard's agentic commerce pages document an Agent Pay integration inside UCP; Mastercard said on 2026-01-20 that it joined Google on UCP and is bringing Agent Pay to Microsoft Copilot Checkout.
Which card network's agentic token, if any, flows inside a Google Pay handler in UCP is not published.
No relation between UCP and ERC-8004 is documented; UCP identity is domain-based through profiles and JWK sets.
MCP and A2A are transport bindings for UCP, not competing commerce protocols.
Mastercard and Visa are listed as UCP endorsers on ucp.dev.
UCP's roadmap lists native cross-sell and upsell modules as a priority.

Google holds a permanent Governing Council seat, the proxy for open seats until December 2028 and custody of ucp.dev; no published critique of this structure was found in trade press or by web search as of 2026-10-20.
The ucp.dev UCP and AP2 page still describes a checkoutSignature and a hashed checkout mandate, which differs from the v2026-08-25 schema.
UCP's attribution field carries campaign parameters such as gclid but does not prescribe an attribution model.
UCP negotiation has two layers: selecting one protocol version profile, then intersecting capabilities by exact version.
The arXiv paper 2606.05043 (Strabo) models UCP checkout as a declarative protocol and reports interoperation with Google's UCP agents.
The arXiv paper 2602.06345 names UCP and AP2 as mandate-based payment authorization protocols and studies replay and context-binding failures.
A UCP session by Amit Handa of Google was on the agenda of the W3C and GS1 workshop on e-commerce for humans and AI agents on 2026-09-08.
The Google Developers blog post Under the Hood: UCP walks through a demo flower shop using the samples and python-sdk repositories.
The UCP glossary says capabilities map 1:1 to MCP tools.
Google's FAQ says that, at launch, UCP integrations power AI Mode in Google Search and the Gemini web and mobile apps.
Google's UCP FAQ says merchants are responsible for real-time inventory checks and must return out_of_stock when an item is unavailable.
The Tokenization API in the UCP repository defines POST /tokenize and POST /detokenize.
Payment handlers advertise available_instruments, and platforms must treat the business-resolved list in the checkout response as authoritative.
The AP2 extension business config example declares vp_formats_supported with dc+sd-jwt.
The checkout REST binding examples name the Shop Pay handler com.shopify.shop_pay, while the overview names it dev.shopify.shop_pay.
The UCP REST binding requires every endpoint to be served over HTTPS with TLS 1.3 or later.
Version 0.5.x of both the JavaScript and the Python UCP SDKs is generated against UCP schema version 2026-08-25.
The Python sample client signs every request with RFC 9421 and an ephemeral ES256 key by default, and serves the matching public key from a local profile.
Checkout messages carry a severity of recoverable, requires_buyer_input, requires_buyer_review or unrecoverable, and the two requires_ severities lead to status requires_escalation.

requires_buyer_input means the business needs data its API cannot collect, while requires_buyer_review means the checkout is complete but a policy needs the buyer to approve it, for example a high-value order.
UCP signature errors are signature_missing, signature_invalid and key_not_found (HTTP 401) and digest_mismatch and algorithm_unsupported (HTTP 400).
If a Complete Checkout response is lost, the platform should poll Get Checkout with bounded backoff and may resend the identical request only with the same idempotency key.
After an Action finishes, the platform must confirm the result with Get Checkout, because the Action completion signal is not authoritative for checkout state.

The AP2 extension allows two signing models: a trusted platform provider signs mandates with its server key after user consent, or the user's wallet signs with a key bound to a digital payment credential, for example through OpenID4VP.
Identity linking errors include identity_required (HTTP 401) and insufficient_scope (HTTP 403) for user-authenticated operations.
A business must provide continue_url on requires_escalation, should provide it for other non-terminal statuses, and should omit it for completed and canceled sessions.

UCP responses carry ucp.status, success or error, which tells the reader whether the body holds the expected resource or error messages; the schema defaults it to success when omitted, and only error responses must set it.
Universal Cart launched in the US on 2026-10-15, rolling out across Google Search and the Gemini app, with checkout powered by UCP; merchants remain the seller of record.
Google said on 2026-09-16 that UCP already enables direct checkout for hundreds of thousands of brands and retailers across Google; the post gives no definition, exact count or transaction volume.
Secondary reports date the automatic enrollment of eligible US Shopify merchants in Google's native checkout to around 2026-09-22, with the rollout starting on 2026-09-18.
Shopify's help center says there are no fees for selling in Google AI Mode and Gemini's direct checkout beyond the merchant's standard payment processing fees.
Microsoft's page says that today Microsoft does not take a commission or affiliate fee on Copilot Checkout transactions, and merchants remain merchant of record.

Shopify's Agentic Storefronts Supplemental Terms (updated 2026-10-06) say that for certain participating channels Shopify may assess a fee on transactions, and that the merchant remains the seller of record.

Google's Merchant Center help (read 2026-10-20) says the UCP integration hub is gradually rolling out in the US, with Australia and Canada to follow next year, and offers cart transfer to a merchant site, native checkout on Google and identity linking; it gives no UK date.
Google's UCP implementation guides cover versions 2026-04-08 and 2026-01-23 only; no guide for v2026-08-25 existed on 2026-10-20.

A draft change merged on 2026-10-16 (PR 659, in no release) requires webhook signatures to also cover webhook-id and webhook-timestamp, requires retries to keep the original Webhook-Id and Webhook-Timestamp, and says platforms should deduplicate on Webhook-Id.
On 2026-10-12 MAINTAINERS.md replaced Harsh Mehta with Simon Farrow of Global Payments on the Payments Tech Council; the list of member companies did not change.

A contributing guide added to ucp.dev on 2026-10-12 defines an Enhancement Proposal lifecycle, three capability maturity levels (Working Draft, Candidate and Stable with a dated version), Governing Council approval plus a 2-week notice for breaking changes, and vendor extensions under com.{vendor}.

Google's UCP FAQ (updated 2026-10-16) lists mutual TLS against Google's UCP root certificate authorities, alongside reverse DNS and published IP ranges, as ways to verify that requests come from Google.

The samples repository marked its A2A business agent and chat client sample unmaintained on 2026-10-15, pending a rewrite tracked in issue 255; the REST Python and Node.js samples received fixes through 2026-10-19.

The release/2026-08-25 branch received a backport on 2026-10-15 (PR 871), so the branch differs from tag v2026-08-25 while ucp.dev still aliases latest to 2026-08-25. The patch marks cart_id as transitioning to omit on complete requests: platforms should not send it and businesses must ignore it.

Google's 2026-10-15 Universal Cart post names Nike, Sephora, Target, Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Wayfair and many Shopify merchants for checkout with Google Pay or cart transfer, without saying which of them have native UCP checkout.

Target's fact sheet (updated 2026-06-18) says shoppers can buy items directly from Target in Google Search, including AI Mode, and the Gemini app, with Google Pay or cart transfer to target.com, and names UCP as what enables it.
In OpenAI's ACP the merchant selling the goods is the merchant of record, not OpenAI; UCP likewise keeps the business as merchant of record, and neither specification maps to the other.
